rows.title: Quality-Aware Decoding: Unifying Quality Estimation and Decoding
rows.domain_tags: machine_translation | quality_estimation | decoding
rows.task_tags: machine_translation | quality_estimation | decoding_optimization
rows.core_contributions: Proposes a token-level, uni-directional Quality Estimation (QE) model that scores partial translations during decoding. | Introduces Quality-Aware Decoding: integrates QE directly into the NMT decoding process—not just as post-hoc re-ranking. | Demonstrates up to +1.39 XCOMET-XXL improvement over N-best re-ranking and shows particular gains in document-level translation.

rows.title: Early-Exit and Instant Confidence Translation Quality Estimation
rows.domain_tags: machine_translation | quality_estimation | uncertainty_quantification
rows.task_tags: translation_quality_estimation | candidate_reranking | confidence_scoring
rows.core_contributions: Introduces Instant Confidence COMET: an uncertainty-aware quality estimation model matching prior methods' performance at much lower computational cost. | Proposes Early-Exit COMET: enables layer-wise early termination during quality estimation, reducing compute by ~50% with minimal performance loss. | Applies Early-Exit COMET with Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) bandit for efficient MT candidate reranking—halving evaluation cost while preserving ranking quality.

rows.title: A Survey of LLM-based Agents in Medicine:How far are we from Baymax?
rows.domain_tags: medicine | healthcare | clinical_ai
rows.task_tags: clinical_reasoning | medical_decision_support | healthcare_optimization | medical_education
rows.core_contributions: Systematic taxonomy of LLM-based medical agent architectures across four dimensions: system profiles, clinical planning, medical reasoning, and external capacity enhancement | Comprehensive review of application scenarios including clinical decision support, documentation, training simulations, and service optimization | Critical analysis of evaluation frameworks, technical challenges (e.g., hallucination), implementation barriers, and ethical concerns in medical agent deployment

rows.title: MM-Verify: Enhancing Multimodal Reasoning with Chain-of-Thought Verification
rows.domain_tags: multimodal reasoning | mathematical reasoning | vision-language models | large language models
rows.task_tags: multimodal mathematical reasoning | visual question answering | multimodal verification
rows.method_tags: chain-of-thought verification | test-time scaling | tree search | rejection sampling | data synthesis | multimodal CoT | LLM-as-a-judge
rows.core_contributions: Introduces MM-Verifier, a dedicated multimodal verifier trained on synthetically generated long-chain-of-thought verification data using tree search and rejection sampling. | Proposes MM-Reasoner, a multimodal reasoner fine-tuned on efficient MMCOT synthesis that bridges text-based and multimodal reasoning. | Achieves SOTA on MathVista (65.3), surpassing GPT-4o (63.8) with 12 rollouts, and outperforms larger models on MathCheck, MathVista, and MathVerse.

rows.title: Beyond Self-Talk: A Communication-Centric Survey of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
rows.domain_tags: multi-agent systems | large language models | artificial intelligence
rows.task_tags: agent coordination | collaborative reasoning | distributed decision-making
rows.core_contributions: Proposes a communication-centric framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems, distinguishing system-level and system-internal communication. | Systematically categorizes communication architectures (flat, hierarchical, team, society, hybrid), goals (cooperation, competition, mixed), strategies (one-by-one, simultaneous-talk, etc.), paradigms (message passing, speech act, blackboard), objects (self, other agents, environment, human), and content (explicit/implicit). | Identifies key open challenges including evaluation benchmarking, multimodal communication, security, scalability, and agent competition research.

rows.title: AIN: The Arabic INclusive Large Multimodal Model
rows.domain_tags: Arabic NLP | multimodal AI | low-resource languages | document understanding | medical imaging | remote sensing
rows.task_tags: visual question answering | handwritten document understanding | video understanding | medical image analysis | remote sensing interpretation
rows.method_tags: bilingual multimodal pretraining | curated multimodal data pipeline | translation-aware data filtering
rows.core_contributions: Introduces AIN: the first bilingual English-Arabic large multimodal model (LMM) designed for inclusive Arabic multimodal understanding. | Constructs and leverages 3.6M high-quality Arabic-English multimodal training samples with rigorous data curation, translation verification, and toxicity filtering. | Achieves SOTA Arabic performance on CAMEL-Bench (outperforming GPT-4o by +3.4% avg. across 38 sub-domains) and ArabicMMLU (+3% overall vs. Qwen2-VL-7B).

rows.title: Predicting Depression in Screening Interviews from Interactive Multi-Theme Collaboration
rows.domain_tags: mental health | clinical NLP | affective computing
rows.task_tags: depression classification | dialogue understanding | thematic analysis
rows.method_tags: in-context learning | theme correlation modeling | interactive feedback simulation | LLM-guided preference learning
rows.core_contributions: Introduces PDIMC, an interactive depression detection framework that explicitly models intra-theme and inter-theme correlations in clinical interview dialogues | Proposes a theme-oriented in-context learning module using LLMs to extract depression-relevant themes while filtering irrelevant dialogue content | Designs an interactive theme adjustment strategy that simulates clinician feedback via LLM-driven preference learning for dynamic theme weighting

rows.title: Transferring Textual Preferences to Vision-Language Understanding through Model Merging
rows.domain_tags: vision-language models | reward modeling | model merging | preference learning
rows.task_tags: multimodal reward assessment | VQA-based reward evaluation
rows.method_tags: model merging | parameter merging | training-free adaptation
rows.core_contributions: Proposes a training-free model merging method to integrate text-based reward models into large vision-language models. | Demonstrates effective transfer of textual preferences to multimodal reward assessment without multimodal preference data or fine-tuning. | Empirically validates improved reward scoring performance over both native LVLM scoring and standalone text-based RMs.

rows.title: Ask in Any Modality:A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
rows.domain_tags: multimodal AI | retrieval-augmented generation | large language models | vision-language models
rows.task_tags: multimodal QA | multimodal fact verification | image-text generation with external knowledge | audio-visual reasoning
rows.method_tags: contrastive multimodal embedding | cross-modal retrieval | multimodal fusion | retrieval-augmented generation
rows.core_contributions: First comprehensive survey systematically organizing Multimodal RAG across datasets, benchmarks, evaluation metrics, and methodological components (retrieval, fusion, augmentation, generation, training) | Structured taxonomy of Multimodal RAG innovations, including contrastive multimodal embedding strategies (e.g., CLIP/BLIP-based), efficient cross-modal retrieval techniques (e.g., MIPS variants, ScaNN, TPU-KNN) | Critical analysis of open challenges: cross-modal alignment, reasoning robustness, agent-based self-guidance, long-context efficiency, and generalization gaps

rows.title: PlotGen: Multi-Agent LLM-based Scientific Data Visualization via Multimodal Feedback
rows.domain_tags: scientific visualization | data science | human-computer interaction
rows.task_tags: data visualization | code generation | self-correction
rows.method_tags: multi-agent system | LLM orchestration | multimodal feedback | self-reflection
rows.core_contributions: Introduces PlotGen, a multi-agent LLM framework for automated scientific visualization | Proposes three multimodal feedback agents (Numeric, Lexical, Visual) enabling iterative self-reflection and refinement | Demonstrates 4–6% improvement over baselines on MatPlotBench and 10–12% quality gain in ablation

rows.title: EmbodiedBench: Comprehensive Benchmarking Multi-modal Large Language Models for Vision-Driven Embodied Agents
rows.domain_tags: embodied_ai | multimodal_learning | robotics | vision_language_models
rows.task_tags: navigation | manipulation | household_task | long_term_planning | spatial_reasoning
rows.core_contributions: Introduces EmbodiedBench: a comprehensive benchmark with 1,128 vision-driven embodied tasks across four environments | Defines six capability-oriented subsets evaluating commonsense reasoning, complex instruction understanding, spatial awareness, visual perception, and long-term planning | Empirically evaluates 19 leading MLLMs, revealing strong performance on high-level tasks but significant gaps (e.g., only 28.9% success for GPT-4o) on low-level navigation and manipulation

rows.title: CounterBench: A Benchmark for Counterfactuals Reasoning in Large Language Models
rows.domain_tags: causal inference | large language models | artificial intelligence | reasoning evaluation
rows.task_tags: counterfactual QA | causal inference | formal reasoning
rows.method_tags: CoIn | iterative reasoning | backtracking reassessment | counterfactual information extraction
rows.core_contributions: Introduces CounterBench, a dedicated benchmark with 1K counterfactual reasoning questions spanning four types (basic, joint, nested, conditional) and diverse causal graph structures. | Empirically demonstrates that current LLMs perform near-randomly on formal counterfactual reasoning — even advanced prompting (e.g., CausalCoT) yields only marginal gains. | Proposes CoIn, a novel iterative reasoning + backtracking paradigm grounded in formal causal inference, which significantly improves counterfactual reasoning across multiple LLMs.

rows.title: CMQCIC-Bench: A Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Medical Quality Control Indicator Calculation
rows.domain_tags: healthcare | clinical NLP | medical AI | quality assurance
rows.task_tags: MQCIC | rule-based clinical reasoning | structured indicator extraction | EMR-to-metric conversion
rows.method_tags: CF-IR | semi-automatic rule enhancement | disentangled reasoning | clinical fact verification | inferential rule reasoning
rows.core_contributions: Introduces CMQCIC-Bench: a Chinese benchmark dataset of 785 EMR-based instances covering 76 medical quality control indicators | Proposes CF-IR (Clinical Facts-based Inferential Rule), a novel reasoning method that disentangles clinical fact verification and inferential rule reasoning | Provides comprehensive evaluation of 20 LLMs on MQCIC, showing CF-IR outperforms Chain-of-Thought and revealing key capability bottlenecks

rows.title: Benchmarking Prompt Sensitivity inLarge Language Models
rows.domain_tags: natural language processing | large language models | prompt engineering
rows.task_tags: prompt sensitivity prediction | question answering | query reformulation robustness
rows.method_tags: prompt sensitivity prediction | query performance prediction | LLM self-evaluation | BERT-based classification
rows.core_contributions: Introduces Prompt Sensitivity Prediction as a new benchmark task to quantify how minor prompt variations affect LLM response correctness. | Releases PromptSET, a novel dataset built on TriviaQA and HotpotQA with systematically generated prompt variations and human- or model-verified answerability labels. | Benchmarks existing methods (LLM self-evaluation, text classification, query performance prediction) and reveals their limitations in predicting prompt sensitivity.

rows.title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
rows.domain_tags: healthcare AI | medical NLP | clinical safety | LLM reliability
rows.task_tags: hallucination detection | fact verification | medical QA evaluation | binary classification
rows.method_tags: hallucination generation pipeline | bidirectional entailment clustering | multi-model majority voting
rows.core_contributions: Introduces MedHallu, the first dedicated benchmark for medical hallucination detection with 10,000 curated question-answer pairs and systematically generated hallucinations. | Proposes a controlled hallucination generation pipeline using multi-model majority voting to mitigate single-LLM bias and enable fine-grained hardness categorization (easy/medium/hard). | Demonstrates that domain knowledge injection and adding a 'not sure' response option significantly improve detection precision and F1 (up to +38% relative gain).

rows.title: Line Goes Up? Inherent Limitations of Benchmarks for Evaluating Large Language Models
rows.domain_tags: LLM evaluation | artificial intelligence assessment | cognitive benchmarking
rows.task_tags: language understanding | reasoning evaluation | scientific reasoning
rows.method_tags: benchmark critique | adversarial evaluation | interpretability analysis
rows.core_contributions: Identifies inherent limitations of the benchmarking paradigm for assessing general LLM cognitive capabilities | Documents empirical evidence of benchmark overfitting and data/task contamination (e.g., SciEval performance drop from 65% to 26%) | Argues for alternative evaluation methods—adversarial stimuli and interpretability techniques—as more reliable indicators of robust, generalisable competence

rows.title: UGPhysics: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Undergraduate Physics Reasoning with Large Language Models
rows.domain_tags: physics | STEM | undergraduate education
rows.task_tags: physics reasoning | multistep reasoning | answer verification
rows.core_contributions: Introduces UGPhysics, a large-scale bilingual (English/Chinese) benchmark with 5,520 undergraduate physics problems across 13 subjects and 7 answer types. | Proposes the MARJ (Model-Assistant Rule-based Judgment) pipeline to robustly evaluate physics answer correctness, addressing precision, unit, and multi-step reasoning challenges. | Provides comprehensive evaluation of 31 LLMs on physics reasoning, revealing low overall accuracy (max 49.8%) and highlighting a critical gap beyond mathematical reasoning.

rows.title: OphthBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Chinese Ophthalmology
rows.domain_tags: Ophthalmology | Chinese medicine | Clinical AI
rows.task_tags: Medical QA | Clinical triage | Diagnosis support | Treatment planning | Prognosis prediction
rows.core_contributions: Introduces OphthBench — the first comprehensive, clinically grounded benchmark for evaluating LLMs in Chinese ophthalmology. | Structures evaluation around five real-world clinical workflow scenarios: Education, Triage, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis, with 9 tasks and 591 questions. | Proposes a dual-prompt evaluation protocol (common-use vs. advanced prompting) and a multi-dimensional LLM-as-Judge scoring method for open-ended questions.

rows.title: SafeDialBench: A Fine-Grained Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Dialogues with Diverse Jailbreak Attacks
rows.domain_tags: LLM safety | responsible AI | adversarial robustness | dialogue systems
rows.task_tags: safety evaluation | adversarial dialogue testing | risk identification in conversation | consistency under attack
rows.method_tags: jailbreak attack injection | multi-turn safety scoring | minimum-score-taking metric | LLM-as-judge + human expert evaluation
rows.core_contributions: Introduces SafeDialBench: a fine-grained, multi-turn dialogue safety benchmark covering 66 safety dimensions and 22 dialogue scenarios in both Chinese and English. | Proposes a two-tier hierarchical safety taxonomy and a novel three-capability evaluation framework (detecting, handling, and maintaining consistency under jailbreak attacks). | Constructs a high-quality dataset with 4000+ multi-turn dialogues using 77 diverse jailbreak attack strategies (e.g., reference attack, purpose reverse).

rows.title: Learning to Generate Unit Tests for Automated Debugging
rows.domain_tags: software engineering | program synthesis | LLM coding
rows.task_tags: unit test generation | automated debugging | code correctness evaluation
rows.method_tags: UTGen | UTDebug | test-time scaling | backtracking validation
rows.core_contributions: Proposes UTGen, a method to jointly generate error-revealing unit test inputs and their correct expected outputs from task descriptions (without gold code). | Introduces UTDebug, a test-time debugging framework that scales UTGen via test-time compute and uses backtracking/validation over multiple generated UTs to avoid overfitting. | Demonstrates UTGen’s superiority as both a unit test generator (7.59% gain) and a correctness judge (4.43% over 8B reward model) on HumanEvalFix and MBPP+.
